beats.text: A student is described by five features: age, G P A, attendance, study hours and income. Five features, so d equals five.
Fewer features means less computation, cheaper data, and simpler models. With two, you can even plot the data.
But fewer features does not promise higher accuracy. What matters is keeping the useful information.
There are two ways to get fewer features. Feature selection keeps some of the original columns. Keep G P A and study hours, and drop the rest. They stay easy to read.
Feature extraction builds new features out of the old ones. Height and weight become one new number: z one equals zero point six times height, plus zero point eight times weight.
How do you choose which columns to keep? Forward search starts with no features. It tries adding each one, and keeps the one with the lowest validation error.
It goes on adding while the error improves. Backward search starts with all of them, and removes. Both are greedy, so neither guarantees the best subset.
The best known extraction method is P C A: principal component analysis.
Here are students' heights and weights. First, centre the cloud, by subtracting the mean.
Now pick a direction, and project every point onto it. Some directions squeeze the points together. Others spread them out.
P C A picks the direction with the greatest spread: the largest variance. That is the first principal component.
The second is perpendicular to the first, and holds the next largest variance. Here the first keeps ninety two percent, and the second the other eight.
On the iris data in the slides, two components keep ninety seven point seven seven percent of the variance.
One trap. P C A never looks at the labels. The direction with the most spread is not always the one that separates the classes.
When separating the classes is the goal, the slides name L D A, which uses the class labels.
For the exam.
Selection keeps original features.
Extraction builds new ones.
Forward search adds. Backward search removes.
P C A keeps the direction of largest variance.
P C A ignores the labels.
